summary: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, create a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that synchronises the two columns bidirectionally, deploy new version state-only, retire old version, and drop the old note column.
write_consistency: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on account_user copies the value of the newly written column to the other column, ensuring that writes from either version are visible to the other version.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because the trigger was created after deploy_new, causing race conditions where writes from the old version during concurrent operation were not synchronised to customer_note, leading to mismatched columns and stale seed data. This revision moves trigger creation before deploy_new, so the sync is active from the start of concurrent operation, and the backfill ensures initial values match. Simple assignment (rather than COALESCE) avoids repeated UPDATE loops.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill existing values, and create sync trigger
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;
UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_trigger BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy new version (new-staged) with state_only migration
Drop old note column after old version retired
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
